speakers.S3: Support worker, Brightwater Advice Project (Moira Quinn)

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Morning, come on through. It's Kayleigh, isn't it? I'm Marcus, Marcus Fenn, from housing options.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, hi. Sorry we're a bit late, the bus, um, the bus just didn't turn up.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: No, honestly, don't worry about it. And you must be from, er, from Brightwater?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Moira, yes. Moira Quinn, from the Brightwater Advice Project. We spoke on the phone last week.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: We did, yeah. Grab a seat. Water? The machine's broken, sorry.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Water's lovely, thanks. It's freezing out there.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So, um, today's a housing needs assessment. Your housing, your money, the family, then what we can do.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Is it okay if Moira stays in for all of it?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, I want her here. I get muddled with the forms and that.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Fine. And are you happy for me to talk to Universal Credit and the landlord's side if I need to?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Go on.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Great. So, who lives with you at the moment?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Just me and the kids. Alfie, he's seven, and Mia, she's three.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And the address is Flat 4, 18 Cobden Street?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: That's it. Top floor. Two bedrooms.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And how long have you been there?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Since, um, the summer of twenty-one. It's private, through Kerridge and Low, the agents. The landlord's a Mr Haskins.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. And was it you and the children's dad on the tenancy?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No, just me on the tenancy. Liam moved in after. He was on the Universal Credit with me though, joint claim.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Right. And Liam's moved out now?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. End of July he went. No, sorry, it was August. It was the day after Alfie's birthday, so the ninth of August.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Ninth of August. Okay.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: And that's where it all went wrong with the money.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I ask everyone this, was there any, um, violence or abuse in the relationship?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. No, nothing like that. He never hurt us. He just left. He's in Bristol now.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. And what's the rent on the flat?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It's eight-fifty a month. Oh, no, wait, it went up in April, didn't it. It's eight-ninety-five now.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Eight-ninety-five, yeah. I've got the increase letter.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Eight-nine-five. And how much does Universal Credit cover?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: The housing bit's seven-two-five. So I'm, um, short a hundred and seventy every month.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Yeah, that's the local housing allowance rate for a two-bed.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Which I could do when Liam was there. But now it's just my wages.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And you're working?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Twelve hours a week. In the kitchen at Cobden Road Primary. I get about, um, six hundred and thirty a month.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Any other income? Child maintenance from Liam, anything?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Nothing. He's not paid a penny since he went. And there's nothing else. No savings, nothing.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Which is why I keep saying get the Child Maintenance Service onto him.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I don't want anything off him, Moira. I'm not chasing him. I just want him gone.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's your call. And child benefit for both?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Oh, yeah, the child benefit. Sorry, didn't think of that as income.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So, the arrears. How much are you behind?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It's about two thousand four hundred.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Is it? I thought the letter said less than that.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Have you got it?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Here, the agent's letter, dated the second of November. It says one thousand nine hundred and sixty.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Oh. Yeah. Nineteen sixty then. The twenty-four was what Liam reckoned, but he's never right.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So one thousand nine hundred and sixty as of the second of November. How did it build up?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: When Liam left, the joint claim got closed and I had to make a new claim, just me.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: And it took like five weeks, so no housing money for, for August or September really.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So two missed months, plus the shortfall. Yeah, that adds up.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Have you ever been in arrears before? Or been evicted from anywhere?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Never. Never been behind before this. And I've never been evicted, no.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: She's been a good tenant. Never missed till this.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Has the landlord or the agent served you any kind of notice?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He keeps texting me. Mr Haskins. Last Tuesday he sent one saying if I don't sort it by the end of the month he'll get his solicitor to serve papers.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Here, look.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Right, the seventeenth of November. Has anything actually come through the door? A notice seeking possession, a solicitor's letter?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Just the texts. Nothing in the post.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So as of today, no notice has been served. That's important.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Even so, given the text and the arrears, I'm opening a prevention case today. We work with you to keep you in the flat.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay. Yeah. Thank you.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: What about temporary accommodation, though? If he did go to court, would they end up somewhere like Fenwick's House?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's a long way off. If it ever got to that point we'd look at it then.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I don't want to go to Fenwick House. I've heard what it's like.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay, the other thing Moira mentioned was the damp.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Oh God. It's in the kids' bedroom, all round the window and down behind Alfie's bed. And the bathroom ceiling's black. Like, black.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How long has it been like that?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Since last winter. Better in the summer, but it's back now, worse.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And have you reported it?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Loads of times. Emailed the agents three times, I think, and rang them.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: I've got copies of the emails. March, June, and the sixth of October.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Has the landlord been in to look at it?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Never. Not once. Not the landlord, not the agent, nobody.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: The girl at Kerridge's, she told me on the phone that Mr Haskins says it's my fault, it's condensation, because I dry the washing in the flat.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Where else am I meant to dry it? There's no dryer.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Which is rubbish anyway, because the bathroom ceiling's been leaking from the roof. That's not washing.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll note that's what the agent said, but we'll get someone qualified to look.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Oh, and the plug socket by Alfie's bed, it sparked last week. It's gone all brown round it. I've put the bed in front of it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Right. That's a concern. Don't use that one at all, okay?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. It's the kids I'm worried about.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Alfie's got asthma. He's on his blue inhaler loads more since it got cold. We ended up in A and E with him in October, the fourteenth.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He's alright now, they gave him steroids. The doctor at the hospital asked if we had damp at home, and I said yeah.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And has a doctor said it's because of the damp?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Nobody's actually said that, no. They just asked. I think it is, but.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: It obviously is.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: We can ask the GP for a letter. That would help.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: And he's, um, Alfie's, they think he might be autistic. The school think so. He's on the waiting list for the assessment.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Has he got a diagnosis?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No, not yet. They said the wait could be eighteen months. But he really struggles with change. Like, new places, he just, he melts down.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's important. So moving him would be a big deal.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Massive. That's why I want to stay where we are. His school's round the corner, he knows the walk.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: I'd disagree a bit, Kayleigh. The flat's not fit to live in. The council should be rehousing you, in a council place.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I know you do. But I don't want to move. I want him to fix it. That's all I want.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll write your wish as staying, with the repairs done. And Moira's view separately.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: That's fair.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And how are you doing, health wise?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I'm alright. I'm on sertaline since the spring, for my depression.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thanks. Are you managing day to day?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Have to, don't I. I've been skipping my tea most nights, to be honest, so they get fed. But it's fine.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: And Mia's fine at nursery, isn't she?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, she loves it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay, what we can do. The arrears first.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I can apply for a discretionary housing payment. A D H P. It's council money for shortfalls and arrears.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: How much do you get?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I can't promise anything. A panel decides whether to award it and how much.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I need three months of bank statements and UC statements by Thursday, and I'll get it in by Friday, the twenty-seventh.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Oh, that's the other thing. My phone's getting cut off on the first of December. I'm behind on the contract.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So how do we get hold of you after that?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Through Moira, probably. Is that alright?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Yeah, of course. Use my work number, it's on the referral.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Contact via Moira from the first. Now, could you pay anything towards the arrears each month?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Maybe, like, fifty? I could do fifty a month. Maybe.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Honestly, I'd hold back the rent until he fixes the place.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. I'm not doing that, Moira. That'll just give him a reason. I want to pay what I owe.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I agree with Kayleigh. Withholding rent would make the arrears worse.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Okay. Okay, I hear you both.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll ring Kerridge and Lowe and put forward fifty pounds a month. It's up to the landlord.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He'll probably say no.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Let's see. Did they say anything else?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: The girl there said he wants to sell the whole building. That's what she said, anyway.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: In writing, or on the phone?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Just on the phone. And she said, um, if I get evicted the council would have to rehouse me straight away anyway, so not to worry.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's not how it works, so don't rely on that.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Repairs. I'll refer the damp, mould and that socket to our private sector housing team, environmental health.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Will he know it was me?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: They'll contact him. But he can't just evict you for complaining about repairs.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay. When would they come out?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I can't give you a date. I'll send the referral by the end of the week and they'll arrange it.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Mrs Patel downstairs said the council came out to her flat last year about damp.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll check the system for the building. I can't see it from here.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: And we'd want a disrepair claim too. Compensation. A year of this with a poorly child.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I don't want to sue him. I just want it fixed. I'll lose the flat.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: It's not suing exactly, it's.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Not now. Please.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Your choice. I'll note Moira raised it and you don't want to go ahead.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Moira, could you get the GP letter about Alfie's asthma and the damp? Millfield Surgery?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Yeah. Give me till the fourth of December, they're slow.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Just so I've asked, if things went badly, is there anyone you could stay with?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: My mum, maybe. In Hull. But she's got a one-bed, and I haven't asked her.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's fine. It's not a plan.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Let me read back.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Prevention case opened today. Statements to me by Thursday. D H P in by Friday the twenty-seventh.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I ring the agent this week about fifty a month. Referral to private sector housing by end of week.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: GP letter by the fourth. And we meet again Monday the seventh. Oh, no, sorry, I'm not in Mondays. Tuesday the eighth, ten o'clock.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Tuesday the eighth. Can you write it down?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll print it. And if a notice or court letter comes, send it to Moira that same day.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And straight on to me.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay. Thank you.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Come on, pick-up.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Thanks, Marcus.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Take care. See you on the eighth.

facts.fact: Housing needs assessment at the council office by Marcus Fenn (housing options, council) with Kayleigh Brennan and her support worker Moira Quinn of the Brightwater Advice Project; Kayleigh wanted Moira present and consented to Marcus contacting Universal Credit and the landlord's side.

Kayleigh lives with her children Alfie (7) and Mia (3) in a two-bedroom, top-floor private rented flat at Flat 4, 18 Cobden Street, where she has been sole tenant since summer 2021; letting agent Kerridge and Lowe, landlord Mr Haskins.

Ex-partner Liam (the children's father) moved out on 9 August 2026; the joint Universal Credit claim closed and her new single claim took about five weeks, so there was no housing payment for roughly August and September.
Rent is £895 a month (increased in April); the UC housing element is £725 (local housing allowance rate for a two-bed), leaving a £170 monthly shortfall she can no longer cover.
Income: about £630 a month from 12 hours a week in the kitchen at Cobden Road Primary, plus Universal Credit and child benefit for both children; no child maintenance, no other income, no savings.
Rent arrears are £1,960 according to the letting agent's letter dated 2 November 2026; she had no arrears before this.

Landlord texted on 17 November threatening to have his solicitor serve papers if arrears are not sorted by the end of the month; no notice has been served, but Marcus opened a homelessness prevention case today.

Damp and black mould in the children's bedroom (around the window, behind Alfie's bed) and on the bathroom ceiling since last winter; reported to the agent by email in March, June and 6 October and by phone; no one has inspected it.
The plug socket by Alfie's bed sparked last week and is scorched brown; Kayleigh has pushed the bed in front of it and was told not to use it.

Alfie has asthma, is using his blue inhaler much more since it got cold, and attended A&E on 14 October (given steroids); he is on the waiting list for an autism assessment (no diagnosis) and struggles badly with change.

Kayleigh's wish is to stay in the flat with the repairs done, because Alfie's school is round the corner and moving would be very hard for him; Moira's differing view (rehousing) is recorded separately.
Kayleigh takes sertraline for depression, since the spring.
Kayleigh has been skipping her evening meal most nights so the children can eat.
Kayleigh's phone will be cut off on 1 December; from then contact her via Moira's work number.

DHP: Kayleigh to provide three months of bank and UC statements by Thursday (26 November); Marcus to submit the discretionary housing payment application by Friday 27 November; a panel decides whether to award and how much.
Marcus will contact Kerridge and Lowe this week to propose repayment of £50 a month towards the arrears; the landlord's response is unknown.
Marcus will refer the damp, mould and the socket to the private sector housing (environmental health) team by the end of the week.
Moira will obtain a GP letter from Millfield Surgery about Alfie's asthma and the damp by 4 December.
Review meeting on Tuesday 8 December at 10am; any notice or court letter must be sent to Moira the same day and on to Marcus.

traps.must_not_claim: Kayleigh experienced violence or abuse from her ex-partner Liam.
traps.note: She explicitly denies any violence or abuse: 'He never hurt us. He just left.'

traps.must_not_claim: Kayleigh receives child maintenance from Liam.
traps.note: She says Liam has not paid a penny since he left; no maintenance, no savings, no other income (child benefit aside).

traps.must_not_claim: Kayleigh has previously been in rent arrears or been evicted.
traps.note: She says she has never been behind before this and has never been evicted.

traps.must_not_claim: Alfie has been diagnosed with autism.
traps.note: He is only on the waiting list for an assessment; asked about a diagnosis she says 'No, not yet.'

traps.must_not_claim: The landlord has served a possession notice (notice seeking possession / Section 8).
traps.note: The landlord only texted that he would get a solicitor to serve papers if not sorted; nothing has come and Marcus confirms no notice has been served.

traps.must_not_claim: The family is to be placed in temporary accommodation at Fenwick House.
traps.note: Moira asked what would happen if it went to court; Marcus said that is a long way off and would be looked at only if it came to that. Kayleigh does not want to go there.

traps.must_not_claim: Kayleigh's mother has agreed to put the family up / Kayleigh plans to move to her mother's in Hull if evicted.
traps.note: Only a possibility raised in answer to 'if things went badly'; her mum has a one-bed, she has not asked her, and Marcus says 'It's not a plan.'

traps.must_not_claim: The damp and mould are caused by condensation from Kayleigh drying washing indoors.
traps.note: This is the landlord's view relayed by an agent's staff member by phone; Moira disputes it (roof leak) and Marcus notes it only as what the agent said, pending a qualified inspection.

traps.must_not_claim: The landlord is selling the building.
traps.note: Only what 'the girl' at the letting agent said on the phone; nothing in writing, unconfirmed.

traps.must_not_claim: The council inspected damp in the building last year.
traps.note: Reported second-hand from neighbour Mrs Patel; Marcus cannot see it on the system and will check.

traps.must_not_claim: Liam moved out at the end of July.
traps.note: Kayleigh corrects herself: he left on 9 August, the day after Alfie's birthday.

traps.must_not_claim: The rent is £850 a month.
traps.note: Corrected immediately: it rose in April and is now £895 a month.

traps.must_not_claim: The rent arrears are about £2,400.
traps.note: The £2,400 was Liam's guess; the agent's letter of 2 November states £1,960, which Kayleigh accepts.

traps.must_not_claim: The review meeting is on Monday 7 December.
traps.note: Marcus corrects himself (not in on Mondays): the review is Tuesday 8 December at 10am.

traps.must_not_claim: A discretionary housing payment has been awarded (or a DHP amount was agreed).
traps.note: The application has not yet been submitted (due by 27 November); a panel decides whether to award and how much. No amount was given.

traps.must_not_claim: A date has been set for the environmental health / private sector housing inspection.
traps.note: Marcus explicitly could not give a date; he will only send the referral by the end of the week.

traps.must_not_claim: The landlord/agent has agreed to a £50-a-month repayment plan.
traps.note: £50 a month is only Kayleigh's offer, which Marcus will put to the agent; it is up to the landlord and his response is unknown.

traps.must_not_claim: A doctor has attributed Alfie's asthma attacks to the damp in the flat.
traps.note: The hospital doctor only asked whether there was damp at home; Kayleigh says nobody has said it is the cause. A GP letter is still to be requested.

traps.must_not_claim: Kayleigh wants to be rehoused into council housing / move out of the flat.
traps.note: Rehousing is Moira's view; Kayleigh says she does not want to move and wants the landlord to fix the flat.

traps.must_not_claim: Kayleigh intends to withhold rent until the repairs are done.
traps.note: Withholding rent was Moira's suggestion; Kayleigh refuses ('I want to pay what I owe') and Marcus agrees with her.

traps.must_not_claim: Kayleigh wants to bring a disrepair compensation claim against the landlord.
traps.note: The disrepair claim is Moira's proposal; Kayleigh declines ('I don't want to sue him... Not now') and Marcus records that she does not want to go ahead.
